claims.statement: Suanggi or suangi, also keswange or iwangi, is a malevolent spirit in the folklore of many regions of Eastern Indonesia.
claims.statement_id: Suanggi atau suangi, juga disebut keswange atau iwangi, adalah roh jahat dalam cerita rakyat berbagai daerah di Indonesia Timur.
claims.quote: Suanggi or Suangi, also known as keswange or iwangi, is a malevolent spirit in the folklore of many regions in Eastern Indonesia.

claims.statement: Suanggi is believed to derive from Greater Central Philippine *aswang ('vampire', 'evil spirit' or 'witch').
claims.statement_id: Suanggi diduga berasal dari kata Greater Central Philippine *aswang ('vampir', 'roh jahat', atau 'penyihir').
claims.quote: Suanggi (also keswange or iwangi) is believed to be derived from Greater Central Philippine *aswang ("vampire," "evil spirit," or "witch").

claims.statement: According to W. R. van Hoëvell, the suanggi is an evil spirit in human shape with magical power to cause disease.
claims.statement_id: Menurut W. R. van Hoëvell, suanggi adalah roh jahat berwujud manusia yang berkekuatan gaib untuk mendatangkan penyakit.
claims.quote: According to W. R. van Hoëvell, Suanggi is an evil spirit in the shape a person having magical power to cause disease and illness.

claims.statement: In Moluccan Malay, suanggi also names villagers suspected of cannibal witchcraft; those deemed proven were killed and their bodies thrown into the sea.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Melayu Maluku, suanggi juga istilah untuk warga yang dicurigai penyihir kanibal; yang dianggap terbukti suanggi dibunuh dan jasadnya dibuang ke laut.
claims.quote: Suanggi is also a Moluccan Malay term for villagers suspected of being cannibal witches. The accusation of being a Suanggi would be fatal, for those who were allegedly proven to be a Suanggi would be killed and their corpses would be thrown into the sea.

claims.statement: After the 1999–2000 conflict in Tobelo, Halmahera, the spirit appeared in February 2004 as a young woman and haunted Tobelo for about two months; identified with O Tokata, a local malevolent spirit, she enticed and then attacked young men.
claims.statement_id: Setelah konflik 1999–2000 di Tobelo, Halmahera, roh ini menampakkan diri pada Februari 2004 sebagai perempuan muda dan menghantui Tobelo sekitar dua bulan; ia disamakan dengan O Tokata, roh jahat setempat, dan memikat lalu menyerang para pemuda.
claims.quote: The spirit manifested itself in February 2004 in the form of a young woman, haunting the Tobelo area for about two months. It was an allegedly unconventional form of Suanggi that was identified with O Tokata, a local malevolent spirit.

claims.statement: This suanggi was claimed to be the vengeful ghost of a girl seeking retribution against her attackers; her presence spread fear in Tobelo and elsewhere in North Maluku.
claims.statement_id: Suanggi ini diklaim sebagai arwah pendendam seorang gadis yang mencari balasan atas penyerangnya; kehadirannya menimbulkan ketakutan di Tobelo dan tempat lain di Maluku Utara.
claims.quote: It was claimed that this Suanggi was the vengeful ghost of a Muslim girl seeking retribution against her attackers.

claims.statement: Suanggi beliefs also exist in East Nusa Tenggara; in 2010-2011 two houses in Adonara, East Flores were destroyed by mobs because their occupants were thought to be suanggi.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan suanggi juga ada di Nusa Tenggara Timur; pada 2010-2011 dua rumah di Adonara, Flores Timur, dirusak massa karena penghuninya dianggap suanggi.
claims.quote: Suanggi beliefs exist in Maluku's neighboring province of East Nusa Tenggara. In 2010-2011, two houses were destroyed by mobs in Adonara, East Flores Regency, due to the occupants being believed to be suanggi.

claims.statement: The apsonsi (อัปสรสีห์) is a half-woman, half-lion mythical creature of Thai mythology, one of many hybrid beings of ancient South and Southeast Asian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Apsonsi (อัปสรสีห์) adalah makhluk mitos setengah perempuan setengah singa dari mitologi Thai, salah satu dari banyak makhluk campuran dalam cerita rakyat kuno Asia Selatan dan Tenggara.
claims.quote: Apsonsi (Thai: อัปสรสีห์) is a half-woman half-lion mythical creature from Thai mythology. Apsonsi is one of the many hybrid creatures depicted in ancient South and Southeast Asian folklore.

claims.statement: It is also called Apsonsingh, Apsonsingha, Apsarasingha or Apsarasingh, a compound of apsara (female nymph) and singha (lion).
claims.statement_id: Apsonsi juga disebut Apsonsingh, Apsonsingha, Apsarasingha, atau Apsarasingh, gabungan apsara (bidadari) dan singha (singa).
claims.quote: Also called Apsonsingh, Apsonsingha, Apsarasingha or Apsarasingh, being the compound of an Apsara (Apson) and a singha (singh), that is a female nymph and a lion.

claims.statement: The male angel-and-lion combination is Thepnorasi; the apsonsi is comparable to the Manussiha, a half-lion, half-man creature of Burma (Myanmar).
claims.statement_id: Gabungan malaikat laki-laki dan singa disebut Thepnorasi; apsonsi dapat dibandingkan dengan Manussiha, makhluk setengah singa setengah manusia dari Myanmar (Burma).
claims.quote: The combination of a male angel and a lion is called Thepnorasi. It is comparable to the Manussiha, a half-lion half-man Burmese mythical creature.

claims.statement: In legend the apsonsi lived in Himavanta, an invisible mythical forest deep in the Himalayas; believed to protect from harm, its figures guard Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha), Bangkok, Thailand.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda apsonsi tinggal di Himavanta, hutan mitos tak kasatmata jauh di Himalaya; ia diyakini pelindung dari marabahaya, dan patungnya berjaga di Wat Phra Kaew (Kuil Buddha Zamrud), Bangkok, Thailand.
claims.quote: In Legend, Apsonsi lived in Himavanta, an invisible mythical forest set deep in the Himalaya Mountains. The Apsonsi is a half-woman, half-lion figure believed to be the protector from harm. Apsonsi figures stand guard at Wat Phra Kaew (The Emerald Buddha Temple), a historic site in Bangkok, Thailand.

claims.statement: Bedawang Nala (ᬩᭂᬤᬯᬂᬦᬮ) is a giant turtle of Balinese mythology carrying the world on its back; in the creation myth it is a transformation of Anantaboga, supports the human world with two nāgas, and its movement causes earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
claims.statement_id: Bedawang Nala (ᬩᭂᬤᬯᬂᬦᬮ) adalah penyu raksasa dalam mitologi Bali yang memikul dunia di punggungnya; dalam mitos penciptaan ia perubahan dari Anantaboga, bersama dua naga menopang dunia manusia, dan bila bergerak terjadi gempa dan letusan gunung berapi.
claims.quote: Bedawang Nala (Bali: ᬩᭂᬤᬯᬂᬦᬮ) adalah seekor penyu raksasa dalam mitologi Bali yang membawa seluruh dunia di punggungnya. Dalam mitologi penciptaan dunia, ia merupakan perubahan dari Anantaboga. Ia bersama dua ular naga mendukung dunia manusia. Jikalau ia bergerak maka akan terjadilah gempa dan letusan gunung berapi di atas bumi.

claims.statement: According to the French Wikipedia, Bedawang belongs to the Balinese Hindu creation myth and was created from the meditation of the cosmic serpent Antaboga.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Prancis, Bedawang termasuk mitos penciptaan Hindu Bali dan tercipta dari semadi ular kosmis Antaboga.
claims.quote: Bedawang fait partie du mythe de la création hindouiste balinais. Il est créé à la suite de la méditation du serpent cosmique Antaboga

claims.statement: Bedawang carries the world, shown with two nāgas, Naga Basuki and Naga Antaboga, representing human needs and acting as stabilizers.
claims.statement_id: Bedawang memikul dunia, digambarkan dengan dua naga, Naga Basuki dan Naga Antaboga, yang melambangkan kebutuhan manusia dan bertindak sebagai penstabil.
claims.quote: figuré par deux nāga (serpents mythiques), Naga Basuki et Naga Antaboga, qui représentent les besoins humains (nourriture, habillement, logement et sécurité) et agissent comme agents stabilisateurs

claims.statement: Sea turtles are hunted and offered in ceremonies with their heads symbolizing Bedawang; to preserve them, Balinese religious leaders decreed a turtle-shaped image or rice cake may be used instead.
claims.statement_id: Penyu laut diburu dan dipersembahkan dalam upacara dengan kepalanya melambangkan Bedawang; untuk melestarikannya, pemuka agama Bali menetapkan gambar atau kue beras berbentuk penyu boleh dipakai sebagai pengganti.
claims.quote: Les tortues de mer sont chassées et données en offrande dans les cérémonies religieuses où leur tête symbolise Bedawang. Pour préserver les espèces de tortues marines, il a été décrété par les chefs religieux balinais qu'une image ou un gâteau de riz en forme de tortue pouvaient être utilisés à la place de l'animal.

claims.statement: The Bukit Timah Monkey Man (BTM) is a cryptid said to inhabit Singapore, chiefly the Bukit Timah forest, cited as a forest hominid or primate and said to be immortal, but its identity is unknown and existence disputed; it is largely considered a product of folklore.
claims.statement_id: Bukit Timah Monkey Man (BTM) adalah kriptid yang konon menghuni Singapura, terutama hutan Bukit Timah, disebut hominid atau primata hutan dan dianggap abadi, tetapi identitasnya tidak diketahui dan keberadaannya diperdebatkan; ia umumnya dianggap produk cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: is a cryptid said to inhabit Singapore, chiefly in the forested Bukit Timah region. The creature is often cited as a forest-dwelling hominid or primate, and is also accounted for as being immortal; however, its exact identity remains unknown, and its existence disputed.

claims.statement: The first report came in 1805, when a Malay elder claimed to see an upright, monkey-faced creature in Bukit Timah.
claims.statement_id: Laporan pertama datang pada 1805, ketika seorang tetua Melayu mengaku melihat makhluk berwajah monyet yang berjalan tegak di Bukit Timah.
claims.quote: The first report of the creature came in 1805, when a Malay elder claimed to have seen an upright-walking, monkey-faced creature in the Bukit Timah area.

claims.statement: In 2007 a series of sightings was reported in the Singapore tabloid The New Paper.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2007 serangkaian penampakan dilaporkan dalam tabloid Singapura The New Paper.
claims.quote: In 2007, a series of sightings were reported in the Singapore tabloid, The New Paper

claims.statement: In late 2020 a night hiker allegedly spotted it, an event widely covered by local media.
claims.statement_id: Pada akhir 2020 seorang pendaki malam mengaku melihatnya, dan peristiwa itu diberitakan luas media setempat.
claims.quote: In late 2020, the Bukit Timah monkey man was allegedly spotted by a night hiker, an event which was extensively covered in local media reports.
